title: Compact-support projection formula at all coefficient stages
statement:
In the six-functor datum of
[def-fix-six-functor-datum], let $f:X\to Y$ be
separated of finite
type, let $K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ and
$L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$, using the
finite-Tor subcategory.
The
projection transformation, built from the
derived tensor and pullback
and the finite-level compact-support direct image of
[def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] and its higher-coefficient versions
[def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support],
is then an isomorphism at every coefficient stage:

$$
\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}:Rf_!K\otimes^L_{\Lambda}L
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf_!\bigl(K\otimes^L_{\Lambda}Lf^*L\bigr),
$$

natural in $K$ and $L$, compatible with the composition law of
[thm-sf-comp-composition] (associativity pentagon), with the compactification comparisons, with
finite reduction on the stated finite-Tor domains and scalar extension,
and with the identification
$Rf_!\cong Rf_*$ for proper $f$. At the rational and algebraically closed stages, when $X=X_0\otimes_{k_0}k$, $Y=Y_0\otimes_{k_0}k$ for separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes and $f$ is the geometric base change of a separated finite-type $k_0$-morphism $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$, the isomorphism restricts to the Weil categories [def-wf-weil-category], with tensor as in [def-wf-tensor-product]. A projection formula for the
derived direct image is asserted
only in the proper case, where it is this same statement via
$Rf_!\cong Rf_*$.

It proves exactly the displayed scalar/tensor, scalar/pullback and support-mate square for every pair of derived inputs and all tensor models. Package the two Nonempty identities together with the universal square as CompactSupportProjectionChange, retaining all original finite-Tor input domains. proof.text: For the stated finite-field model, [lem-sf-projection-weil-tensor-domain-bridge] identifies the tensor models and verifies all constructible domains. [lem-fix-weil-operations] therefore makes PF equivariant. In [def-wf-weil-category], its underlying inverse is equivariant: from $u\varphi_S=\varphi_T\Phi^*u$ obtain $\varphi_S\Phi^*(u^{-1})=u^{-1}\varphi_T$. At a common finite field the same inverse defines the inverse class. Naturality remains an equality of Weil morphisms.

proof.text: The completed-Frobenius integral membership follows by transporting pbcIsoAmbientPullback_preserves across pbcIsoCompletedPullback_identification. The finite comparison functor identity gives equality of carriers. Forgetting the actual finite-equivalence counit gives the uniquely normalized cancellation iso, since the raw arrow determines an isomorphism uniquely.

source.place: Weil-equivariance clause; existing coefficient transport and equivalence-counit assembly, S4 2026-10-25

proof.text: The concrete tensor comparison is assembled by the generic three-arrow composite projectionTensorArrowAssembly. It applies the recorded coefficient tensor comparison, the ordinary tensor map of the two uniquely normalized cancellation arrows, and R.chi. This refactor preserves that fixed composite while checking its category operations abstractly.

For CompactSupportPbcProjection.forward, apply CompactSupportWeilProjection.restriction to the inverse coefficient presentations of the two input Weil objects. Map that isomorphism through the finite fixed-pair coefficient functor and then the exact/completed bridge functor. The finite_functors equality identifies the first underlying map with the rational coefficient image; the bridge functor is induced by the identity on the coefficient category and leaves the underlying arrow unchanged. The defining equation from restriction therefore gives exactly the prescribed underlying projection arrow. Two candidate isomorphisms with this arrow have equal homs by the faithful full-subcategory and algebra forgetful maps, and hence are equal by Iso.ext. The underlying-map calculation is checked first over abstract categories and then specialized to the recorded coefficient datum. The isomorphism witness and uniqueness argument are written explicitly in this module; no new existence obligation is introduced.

source.place: Weil-equivariance sentence; transport of the existing fixed-pair projection through the normalized coefficient comparison.

proof.text: The structural laws of the projection maps (naturality, compactification independence, composition, pentagon and the proper identification) at every coefficient stage are [prop-sf-pf-coherence]; this statement records them with the invertibility.

blueprint_update.statement:
In the six-functor datum of
[def-fix-six-functor-datum], let $f:X\to Y$ be
separated of finite
type, let $K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ and
$L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$, using the
finite-Tor subcategory.
The
projection transformation, built from the
derived tensor and pullback
and the compact-support direct image of
[def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed],
is then an isomorphism for every admissible coefficient ring:

$$
\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}:Rf_!K\otimes^L_{\Lambda}L
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf_!\bigl(K\otimes^L_{\Lambda}Lf^*L\bigr),
$$

natural in $K$ and $L$, compatible with the composition law of
[thm-sf-comp-composition] (associativity pentagon), with the compactification comparisons, with
finite reduction on the stated finite-Tor domains and scalar extension,
and with the identification
$Rf_!\cong Rf_*$ for proper $f$; for $\Lambda=E,\Qlb$ it is compatible
with Weil structures: for Weil complexes in the sense of
[def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], with the tensor Frobenius of
[def-wf-tensor-product], it is a morphism of Weil complexes
([lem-fix-weil-operations]). A projection formula for the
derived direct image is asserted
only in the proper case, where it is this same statement via
$Rf_!\cong Rf_*$.

proof.text:
The geometric-fiber argument of
[lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula] proves the finite
coefficient formula. The compatibility of the specified maps under
successive coefficient reductions is [prop-sf-pf-reduction], applied to
$\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ and the ideal $J=\pi_E^mA_{E,n}$, for which the reduction
modulo $J$ is $K\mapsto K\otimes^L_{A_{E,n}}A_{E,m}$.
Thus [thm-sf-pf-adic] reconstructs the integral map, and
[thm-sf-pf-field] transports it to the field stages; this transport is the
compatibility with scalar extension.
The site comparison of [thm-sf-pf-proetale] gives the stated
pro-etale realization. The composition, refinement, exchange and
proper-coincidence identities are [prop-sf-pf-coherence].
Its equivariance for Weil complexes is the equivariance of the
projection transformation in [lem-fix-weil-operations].
Every step constructs or compares the same projection map; none
uses smooth purity or Verdier duality.
